title: Part 5 replay.json (simon.replay.v1)
description: Both normalised skeletons, matched frame for frame, for a 3D replay. Written by `part5 analyse --replay`. The timeline runs on the expected clip's frames: at expected frame i the follower shows its own file's frame exp_to_fol[i]. Times are seconds as written in each input file. Extra fields are allowed. 1.1.0 (TICKET-085): every new replay says where the alignment path ends. The alignment is open-ended, so the follower may go on after the routine: the follower frames after follower_t[max(exp_to_fol)] were never compared or scored. aligned_until_s is that time and aligned_until_expected_frame the last expected frame shown with it. A reader that maps follower frames back to expected ones would pair every later follower frame with that expected frame; leave those frames out instead (keep the follower frames whose follower_t is at most aligned_until_s). Reported only: the alignment, the faults and the score are what they were. A 1.0.0 replay has neither field and still validates.

joints.description: The 17 canonical joint names, in order.

aligned_until_s.description: 1.1.0 (TICKET-085): seconds on the follower file's own clock, follower_t at the largest exp_to_fol index: where the alignment path ends. Follower frames after it are the idle tail the open-ended alignment skipped; they were never compared or scored. Equal to follower_t[-1] when the path reaches the follower's last frame.

aligned_until_expected_frame.description: 1.1.0 (TICKET-085): the index into expected (and expected_t) of the last expected frame shown with the follower frame at aligned_until_s, the last index of exp_to_fol that holds its largest value.

frames.description: Per frame, 17 joints: [x, y, z] metres (4 decimals) or null where the joint is missing.
